fact: In the D=0 branch, for arbitrary t,u∈I and φ(t)=(x_0,t), the stipulated Euclidean product metric gives d(φ(t),φ(u))²=|t-u|², hence d(φ(t),φ(u))=|t-u|.
justification: The first-coordinate distance d(x_0,x_0) is zero by the stipulated metric structure. Write a=d(φ(t),φ(u)) and b=|t-u|; both are nonnegative. The product formula gives a²=b². If a+b=0, both vanish; otherwise a+b>0 and (a-b)(a+b)=0 gives a=b. This is routine ordered-field expansion of the displayed distance calculation, not an additional isometry theorem or a changed proof route.
